summary: The milestone completed 11 experiments in 3.4 minutes, including 5 compute-bound experiments. Exclusive full-load ARC preflight and teardown receipt was the longest listed compute task at 1.63 minutes, followed by Procedural versus trace memory prospective A/B at 1.0 minute; no data available this milestone identifies why they took longest.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction does not attribute elapsed time to launch, model load, inference, or teardown phases, so the cause of the longest compute durations is unknown.
The GPU report is a point-in-time host snapshot rather than task-owned telemetry, limiting per-experiment utilization analysis even though the locked compute-idle indicator is false.
No data available this milestone records concurrent model count or runner identity, so DualGPURunner eligibility and engagement cannot be evaluated.
improvements_suggested: Emit task-owned monotonic timestamps for launch, model load, inference, artifact write, and teardown phases.
Attach sampled GPU utilization, process identity, device assignment, model count, and runner identity to each compute experiment receipt.
Add device-aware queue scheduling that may place a separate ready single-model experiment on an idle second GPU without requiring DualGPURunner for single-model tasks.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Replace disk-mtime-only reconstruction with task-owned monotonic phase timing.
Record per-task accelerator samples, model concurrency, runner identity, and device assignment in launch receipts.
Use device-aware scheduling for independent ready compute experiments when another GPU is idle.
meta_reflection: GPU 0 was actively utilized while the locked compute-task idle indicator remained false, so GPU idle is not identified as a bottleneck. No data available this milestone shows a compute-bound task loading two or more models in parallel, so no DualGPURunner failure can be claimed; the proposed tooling would make both phase cost and runner applicability directly observable.
